sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This visa lets you stay lawfully in Australia while you make arrangements to leave, finalise your immigration matter or wait for an immigration decision.

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- comply with all Australian laws
- be in Australia when the application is lodged and in order to be granted this visa, you must be in Australia when a decision is made.

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa you can
sections.text: - stay in Australia lawfully while you finalise your immigration matter or make arrangements to leave Australia

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text: For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > Types of bridging visas
sections.text:
You can stay in Australia lawfully while you finalise your immigration matter or make arrangements to leave Australia.

There are two types of BVEs:

- Bridging (General) visa (subclass 050) - generally if you are currently unlawful, the holder of a BVE 050 or the holder of a BVD 041
- Bridging (Protection Visa Applicant) visa (subclass 051) - used in limited situations. This allows certain eligible non-citizens (as specified by the Regulations) to remain lawfully in Australia while their protection visa application is finalised

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa you can
sections.text:
You can stay in Australia if:

- you are making arrangements to leave Australia
- you are applying for a substantive visa
- you are seeking merits or judicial review of a visa decision or citizenship decision
- you are seeking ministerial intervention

When you apply for this visa, you must be:

- an unlawful non-citizen
- the holder of a BVE (subclass 050) or
- the holder of a Bridging D visa (BVD) (subclass 041).

Working in Australia while you hold a BVE

Your grant letter will tell you if you are allowed to work. If you work when you are not allowed to, we can:

- cancel your BVE
- detain you
- remove you from Australia.

If you are not allowed to work, there are only some situations where you might be able to apply for a new BVE that does allow you to work. For example, you might be in financial hardship if you cannot pay for the reasonable cost of your living expenses.

We will assess your situation to see if you meet the requirements. If you do not meet the requirements we will not grant you a new BVE that allows you to work.

There are different requirements, depending on whether you have applied for judicial review or ministerial intervention. There are also special rules for when protection visa applicants are allowed to work.

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This visa is valid until a specified date, or for a particular time period, or a specified event happens.

Your BVE will also end if:

- you leave Australia
- we grant you a substantive visa
- we grant you another Bridging visa in relation to the same matter that your current BVE is associated with
- your BVE is cancelled.

Your grant letter will tell you if your visa has an expiry date. You can also check this information in VEVO.

In other situations, your BVE will cease when a specified event happens.

If your Bridging visa relates to an ongoing visa application

BVE granted on or after 19 November 2016

Your BVE will cease 35 calendar days after:

- our refusal decision or a decision by the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) (or equivalent) in relation to your associated substantive visa application
- a determination that your substantive visa application or an application for review by the ART is invalid
- you withdraw your substantive visa application or application for review by the ART

BVE granted before 19 November 2016

Your BVE will cease 28 days after the date that one of the following happens:

- we notify you that your substantive visa application is not valid or has been refused
- a merits review tribunal notifies you that it has upheld our decision to refuse your substantive visa application or that it has no jurisdiction to consider your application for review
- you withdraw your substantive visa application or application for review by the ART

If your Bridging visa relates to ongoing judicial review

Your BVE will cease 28 calendar days after:

- the judicial review proceedings are complete
- you withdraw your judicial review application

If your Bridging visa relates to another matter

There are other events that may occur where your Bridging visa is connected to a different matter such as a revocation application or while awaiting another person's review process. When your visa ends may depend on what happens in that person's matter.

Check your visa status in VEVO if:

- you (or the other person) have been notified of an outcome on your application or review
- you (or the other person) withdraw an application or review
- the ART or a court determines your matter should be reconsidered by the ART or department
- you are granted another visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Stay longer
sections.text:
You cannot stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. You will need to apply for a new BVE or explore other visa options if you are:

- unable to leave Australia, or
- unable to resolve your immigration matter

before your visa expires.

Explore your visa options.

If you are unsure about your options or need help to resolve your immigration status, you can seek assistance from the Status Resolution Service and Meet with us.

If you are unable to depart due to financial hardship, you can access help. Find out more at Help to leave Australia.

sections.heading: About this visa > Apply from
sections.text: You and anyone included in your application must be in Australia when the BVE application is lodged. To be granted the BVE, you and anyone else included in your application must be in Australia when the decision is made.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You and anyone included in your application must:

- comply with all Australian laws
- be in Australia when the application is lodged and granted

sections.heading: About this visa > Travel
sections.text: A BVE allows you to stay in Australia lawfully for a short time. It will end immediately if you leave Australia. You will not be able to return unless you have another visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa label
sections.text: We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text:
You must meet all of the following eligibility criteria to be eligible for this visa under the Temporary Residence Transition stream.
Answer the questions below to see if you meet them, and which requirements that apply to you.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be an unlawful non-citizen or hold a BVE (subclass 050) or hold a BVD (subclass 041)
sections.text: You must be an unlawful non-citizen, the holder of a BVE (subclass 050) or the holder of a Bridging visa D (BVD) (subclass 041), when you apply for this visa, and 1 of the following must apply to you:

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be an unlawful non-citizen or hold a BVE (subclass 050) or hold a BVD (subclass 041) > Be making arrangements to leave Australia
sections.text: You must be making arrangements to depart Australia.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be an unlawful non-citizen or hold a BVE (subclass 050) or hold a BVD (subclass 041) > Be applying for a substantive visa
sections.text: You must be applying for a substantive visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be an unlawful non-citizen or hold a BVE (subclass 050) or hold a BVD (subclass 041) > Be applying for merits or a judicial review
sections.text: You must be seeking merits or judicial review of a visa decision or citizenship decision, or be seeking ministerial intervention.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Age
sections.text: You can be any age to apply for this visa. If you are under 18 years of age please apply on an application with your parent/guardian.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet character requirement
sections.text:
You must meet our character requirement.

We might also ask that other family members meet the requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Previously refused application or a cancelled visa
sections.text: Check if visa cancellation affects your eligibility.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
A BVE application cannot be made in anticipation of becoming unlawful. You must be an unlawful non-citizen, BVE holder or BVD holder. If your substantive visa is still in effect, look at other visa options first and only apply for a BVE once your substantive visa has expired.

In some cases, when you make a valid application for a substantive visa in Australia, you will also have applied for a BVE. We will tell you if this happens. In this case, you do not need to lodge a separate application.

You should read about this visa, understand what it lets you do and the eligibility criteria first.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner, or
- an exempt person.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents
sections.text:
Gather the documents you need for your application.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Provide accurate documents
sections.text: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you cannot prove your identity or do not provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
Provide colour copies of the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide:

- a national identity card, if you have one
- proof of change of name

Documents that prove a change of name include:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Supporting documents
sections.text:
Provide documents to support your application for the visa.

Include details of any immigration matters you are awaiting the outcome of, including:

- visa applications
- merit review proceedings
- judicial review proceedings
- ministerial intervention requests

Or, if you are applying for the visa because you are arranging your departure from Australia, provide details of:

- when you intend to leave
- where you are going
- your current passport or other travel document
- your ticket

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text: We will tell you if and when you need to get a police certificate.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount if you applied online, or send with your paper application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

Note: You do not need to have any documents certified.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Scan or photograph
sections.text:
Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

The scans and photos must be clear.

If a document is more than 1 page, save it all as 1 file.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Keep
sections.text: Keep a copy of your completed application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa
sections.text:
The preferred method is to apply online.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply online
sections.text:
You and anyone included in your application must be in Australia when you lodge the BVE application.

You can apply for a BVE if you do not already have an undecided BVE application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply on paper
sections.text:
Complete Form 1008 Application for Bridging visa E - subclass 050.

Send your paper application by post to the Australian Visa and Citizenship Office nearest to you, as you might need to attend an interview as part of the application process.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
See what you can and must do after you apply.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > What will happen after you apply
sections.text: We will let you know when we have received your application and documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Status updates
sections.text:
We can't give updates on applications.

Wait for us to contact you.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel
sections.text:
A BVE lets you temporarily stay in Australia. It will end when you leave Australia. If you travel outside Australia after you apply for a BVE, you need a visa to return.

But, in order to be granted this visa, you and anyone included in your application must be in Australia when we make a decision.

Learn about visa expiry.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: We will let you know if you need health examinations.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photo). We will let you know if you need to provide them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Attach more information
sections.text:
If you did not attach all documents when you applied, attach them as soon as possible in ImmiAccount.

If you applied on paper, send the documents to the office where you lodged the application.

We might also ask you to provide more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount if you applied online, or send to the office where you submitted your application.

For more information see Who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Things you need to let us know about after you have applied include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- the birth of a child
- you want to withdraw your application

See how to tell us if your situation changes.

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will tell you when we make a decision about your visa application in writing.

In order to be granted a BVE, you and anyone included in your application must be in Australia when we make a decision.

We will let you know in writing our decision about your visa application. If we grant you a BVE, the notification letter will tell you:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions

Keep a copy of the letter with you when in Australia.

If we refuse your visa, we will let you know in writing. We will tell you:

- why it was refused
- whether you have a right to a review of the decision

New step description

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
What you can do when you have this visa

- stay lawfully in Australia until a decision is made on your substantive visa application

To see your specific conditions use VEVO.

What you must do on this visa (your obligations)

- comply with all Australian laws
- comply with all conditions (if any) on this visa

Tell us if things change

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- you want to withdraw your application

See how to let us know if there is a change in your situation.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

At the Border

Leaving the airport faster

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

After you leave

International Movement Record

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > You must
sections.text: - You need to be holding a subclass 457 visa

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > How long you can stay
sections.text: This is a permanent visa. You can stay in Australia indefinitely
